osps_ac_01_01_justification: The brazilian-utils GitHub organization requires two-factor authentication for every member, enforced by GitHub.
osps_ac_02_01_justification: GitHub requires a role to be chosen for every new collaborator and the organization's base permission is Read; https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md#becoming-a-maintainer grants the lowest access first.
osps_ac_03_01_justification: Branch protection on main requires a pull request for every change.
osps_ac_03_02_justification: Branch protection on main blocks deletion of the branch.
osps_br_01_01_justification: Workflows are linted on every pull request with actionlint and zizmor (template injection included): https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/.github/workflows/security.yml
osps_br_01_03_justification: Pull requests run on the pull_request event with a read-only token, no secrets for forks and persist-credentials: false; publishing runs only on main: https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml
osps_br_03_01_justification: Every official channel is HTTPS only: https://brazilian-utils.com.br, https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript and https://www.npmjs.com/package/@brazilian-utils/brazilian-utils
osps_br_03_02_justification: Releases are distributed by the npm registry over TLS, published with provenance (Sigstore) through npm Trusted Publishing.
osps_br_07_01_justification: GitHub secret scanning with push protection is enabled, TruffleHog scans every pull request (https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/.github/workflows/security.yml) and .env files are git-ignored.
osps_do_01_01_justification: https://brazilian-utils.com.br/getting-started and https://brazilian-utils.com.br/utilities document every utility, in English and Portuguese.
osps_do_02_01_justification: https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/SUPPORT.md and the bug report issue template: https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/issues/new/choose
osps_le_02_02_justification: The npm package is released under the same MIT license (license field in package.json).
osps_le_03_02_justification: npm always includes the LICENSE file in the published tarball, and package.json declares MIT.
osps_qa_02_01_justification: https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/package.json and https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/package-lock.json (the published package has zero runtime dependencies).
osps_qa_04_01_justification: The project is a single repository.
osps_qa_05_01_justification: Build output (dist) is git-ignored; nothing generated and executable is committed.
osps_qa_05_02_justification: The only binary files are two small PNG images of the docs site (docs/images), reviewable as images.
osps_ac_04_01_justification: Every workflow declares top-level permissions: contents: read, so a job without its own block gets read-only access: https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/tree/main/.github/workflows
osps_br_02_01_justification: Semantic versions assigned by release-please, one git tag and GitHub Release per version: https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/releases
osps_br_04_01_justification: Release notes and CHANGELOG.md are generated from Conventional Commits: https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
osps_br_05_01_justification: Dependencies are installed with npm ci from the committed package-lock.json, checked by lockfile-lint.
osps_br_06_01_justification: Each release is published to npm with a provenance attestation signed through Sigstore (npm stage publish --provenance): https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-a-release
osps_do_07_01_justification: https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#getting-started and the Development section of the README.
osps_gv_03_02_justification: https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md (adding a utility, lint and type strictness, code quality gates, commit messages, submitting a pull request).
osps_le_01_01_justification: The DCO sign-off is documented in https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#commit-messages but no check enforces it yet, and recent commits carry no Signed-off-by line.
osps_qa_03_01_justification: Branch protection on main requires the status checks to pass before a merge (Check, Build, the Node.js, Bun, Deno and Chrome test jobs, workflow lint, OSV-Scanner and CodeQL); only an administrator can bypass them, explicitly.
osps_qa_06_01_justification: The Tests workflow runs the suite on Node.js 20/22/24/26, Bun, Deno and four browsers on every pull request: https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/.github/workflows/tests.yml
osps_sa_02_01_justification: The public API is documented at https://brazilian-utils.com.br/utilities and checked on every pull request against the last npm release, which fails on a breaking change and lists every added, removed and changed declaration: https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#public-api-validation
osps_vm_03_01_justification: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled: https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/security/advisories/new
osps_vm_04_01_justification: Vulnerabilities are published as GitHub Security Advisories: https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/security/advisories (see https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/SECURITY.md#disclosure).
osps_ac_04_02_justification: Jobs that need more than read access declare only what they use (pull-requests: write for the PR comment, id-token: write for npm OIDC, security-events: write for SARIF): https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml
osps_br_01_04_justification: workflow_dispatch triggers take no inputs, and zizmor checks every workflow for injection on each pull request.
osps_br_02_02_justification: The npm tarball carries the version, and the SBOM artifact of each release run is named after its tag (sbom-<tag>).
osps_do_03_02_justification: https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-a-release (the provenance attestation names the repository and the release workflow that built the package).
osps_do_05_01_justification: https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions (only the latest major receives security updates; versions below 2.0 do not).
osps_qa_02_02_justification: A CycloneDX SBOM (brazilian-utils.cdx.json) is generated by the release workflow and shipped inside the npm package.
osps_qa_04_02_justification: The project is a single repository.
osps_qa_06_03_justification: https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#submitting-a-pull-request (pull requests without tests for new behavior are not merged; 100% coverage and mutation score thresholds).
osps_qa_07_01_justification: Pull requests are required, but branch protection asks for zero approvals today, so a maintainer can merge their own change.
osps_vm_04_02_justification: https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/openvex.json, checked against the suppression lists on every pull request (npm run check:vex).
osps_vm_05_02_justification: https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/SECURITY.md#dependency-and-static-analysis-policy (no high or critical advisory may be merged or released).
osps_vm_05_03_justification: audit-ci (in the required Check job) and OSV-Scanner (a required check) evaluate every pull request against https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/SECURITY.md#dependency-and-static-analysis-policy and block the merge; suppressions are declared in the allow list and in https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/openvex.json
osps_vm_06_02_justification: CodeQL, oxlint/TypeScript (the Check job), actionlint and zizmor run on every pull request as required status checks and block the merge on a finding, per https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/SECURITY.md#dependency-and-static-analysis-policy
description_good_justification: The README and https://brazilian-utils.com.br describe what the library does and the problems it solves.
interact_justification: The README links to the documentation, the issue tracker and CONTRIBUTING.md.
documentation_interface_justification: https://brazilian-utils.com.br/utilities documents every exported function; API Extractor fails CI on an undocumented export: https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#public-api-validation
sites_https_justification: The site, the repository and the npm package are HTTPS only.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues and Discussions, searchable and open to anyone: https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/discussions
english_justification: Code, docs and issues are in English; the docs are also translated to Portuguese.
maintained_justification: Actively maintained: 2.4.0 released in September 2026, with commits and merged pull requests every week.
repo_interim_justification: Every change lands on main through a pull request between releases.
version_unique_justification: Each release has a unique semantic version, git tag and npm version.
version_semver_justification: Semantic Versioning, computed by release-please from Conventional Commits.
version_tags_justification: Each release is a git tag: https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/tags
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerability has been fixed in a release so far; the release notes would name it.
report_responses_justification: Every bug report opened in the last 12 months was answered and closed: https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/issues?q=is%3Aissue
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests of the last 12 months were answered (e.g. #441, #442, #459, #460).
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/security/advisories/new (GitHub private vulnerability reporting) or the email in https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability report was received in the last 6 months; SECURITY.md commits to an acknowledgement within 3 business days.
build_floss_tools_justification: Node.js, npm, TypeScript and Vite+ are all FLOSS.
test_justification: Vitest suite, about 6,100 tests: npm test. https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#getting-started
test_invocation_justification: npm test, the standard for npm packages.
test_most_justification: 100% statement, branch, function and line coverage is enforced, plus a 100% mutation score (Stryker).
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions run the suite on every pull request and push: https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/.github/workflows/tests.yml
test_policy_justification: https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#submitting-a-pull-request: pull requests without tests for new behavior are not merged.
tests_are_added_justification: Recent changes ship with tests, e.g. https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/pull/547; the coverage thresholds fail CI otherwise.
warnings_justification: TypeScript strict mode and oxlint with type-aware rules, the correctness, suspicious, perf and pedantic categories as errors, plus SonarJS.
warnings_fixed_justification: Every lint and type finding fails the Check workflow, so main has none.
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainers wrote the threat model and the security policies in https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/SECURITY.md#threat-model
know_common_errors_justification: The threat model covers injection through workflows, prototype pollution, ReDoS-style hangs, supply-chain and credential compromise, each with its mitigation.
crypto_published_justification: The library implements no cryptography: it validates, formats, parses and generates Brazilian identifiers.
crypto_call_justification: The library implements no cryptography: it validates, formats, parses and generates Brazilian identifiers.
crypto_floss_justification: The library implements no cryptography: it validates, formats, parses and generates Brazilian identifiers.
crypto_keylength_justification: The library implements no cryptography: it validates, formats, parses and generates Brazilian identifiers.
crypto_working_justification: The library implements no cryptography: it validates, formats, parses and generates Brazilian identifiers.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: The library implements no cryptography: it validates, formats, parses and generates Brazilian identifiers.
crypto_pfs_justification: The library implements no cryptography: it validates, formats, parses and generates Brazilian identifiers.
crypto_random_justification: The library generates no keys or nonces; the generate* utilities are documented as Math.random based fixtures, not for security use.
delivery_mitm_justification: Distributed by the npm registry over HTTPS, with a provenance attestation.
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hash is retrieved over HTTP; npm verifies the integrity hash and the registry signature over HTTPS.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: The published package has zero runtime dependencies and no known vulnerability. The two open advisories are in a development-only dependency and are recorded as not_affected in https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/openvex.json
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerability has been reported; the policy requires a fix before any release.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: Secret scanning with push protection and TruffleHog on every pull request; publishing uses OIDC, so there is no npm token to leak.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL, oxlint (type-aware, with SonarJS), TypeScript strict, knip, jscpd, actionlint and zizmor run on every pull request.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL with the JavaScript/TypeScript security queries.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Findings block the merge; there are no open code scanning alerts of medium or higher severity.
static_analysis_often_justification: On every pull request and push, plus a weekly scheduled run.
dynamic_analysis_justification: Property-based testing with fast-check feeds every utility arbitrary and adversarial input on every CI run, and Stryker mutation testing runs on every pull request.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The library is made of small pure functions and ships no run-time assertions; the properties are asserted by the test suite instead.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: A failing property is fixed before merging, e.g. https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/pull/547
dco_justification: The DCO sign-off is documented in https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#commit-messages but not enforced by a check yet.
access_continuity_justification: The GitHub organization has four owners with admin access and the npm package three owners, so any of them can merge, close issues and approve a release: https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md
bus_factor_justification: One maintainer wrote most of the 2.x line, so the bus factor is 1 today: https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/graphs/contributors
documentation_roadmap_justification: There is no published roadmap yet.
documentation_current_justification: The docs are checked in CI: the Check workflow rebuilds llms.txt from them on every run, so a doc the generator cannot read fails it, jsr.json fails it when stale, an undocumented export fails the public API check, and a pull request that changes a utility must update both language versions.
documentation_achievements_justification: The README links the OpenSSF Best Practices and Scorecard badges: https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript#readme
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: The library has no user interface; the documentation site has not been audited for accessibility.
internationalization_justification: The library returns data, not user-facing text; the utilities that produce words (convertNumberToWords and friends) are Brazilian Portuguese by design. The docs are in English and Portuguese.
sites_password_security_justification: The project sites store no passwords; authentication is GitHub's and npm's.
maintenance_or_update_justification: 1.x names are kept as deprecated aliases in 2.x and the upgrade is documented: https://brazilian-utils.com.br/migration-v1-to-v2
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: No vulnerability was resolved in the last 12 months; SECURITY.md commits to crediting reporters.
coding_standards_enforced_justification: vp check (oxfmt formatting, oxlint, TypeScript) runs in the Check workflow and blocks the merge.
build_preserve_debug_justification: No native build; source maps are shipped with the package.
build_non_recursive_justification: A single package built by one bundler invocation.
build_repeatable_justification: Two clean builds of the same commit produce byte-identical output (all 690 files of dist compared by SHA-256).
installation_common_justification: npm install / npm uninstall (also yarn, pnpm and bun).
installation_standard_variables_justific: Installed by the package manager into node_modules; the project has no installer of its own.
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot, audit-ci and OSV-Scanner on every pull request and weekly; exceptions are recorded in openvex.json.
updateable_reused_components_justificati: Zero runtime dependencies; development dependencies come from npm and are pinned by the lockfile.
interfaces_current_justification: The typescript/no-deprecated lint rule is an error, and CI runs on the current Node.js, Bun and Deno releases.
automated_integration_testing_justificat: The Tests workflow runs on every pull request and push to main and reports per job: https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/actions/workflows/tests.yml
regression_tests_added50_justification: Bug fixes land with a regression test (e.g. #547 replays the failing seed), and the 100% coverage and mutation thresholds require it.
test_statement_coverage80_justification: 100% statement coverage, enforced in CI and reported to Codecov.
implement_secure_design_justification: Pure functions with no I/O except two HTTPS lookups, zero runtime dependencies, input validated before use, no eval or dynamic code, least-privilege CI: https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/SECURITY.md#threat-model
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: The library implements no cryptography: it validates, formats, parses and generates Brazilian identifiers.
crypto_credential_agility_justification: The library handles no credentials or keys.
crypto_used_network_justification: The only network calls (the CEP lookups) use HTTPS endpoints exclusively.
crypto_tls12_justification: TLS is provided by the runtime's fetch (Node.js, Bun, Deno, browsers), all of which support TLS 1.2 and later.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: The runtime's fetch verifies certificates by default and the library never disables it.
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: No private headers or cookies are sent; verification happens in the runtime before any request data is sent.
signed_releases_justification: Releases are published to npm with a Sigstore-signed provenance attestation; verification is documented in https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-a-release
version_tags_signed_justification: Tags are created by release-please through the GitHub API and are not GPG-signed.
input_validation_justification: Every utility validates its input against the documented format (allowlist regexes and check digits) and returns false, an empty string or null for anything else; property tests assert it for arbitrary input.
hardening_justification: A library of pure functions: there is no binary, server or HTTP response to harden.
assurance_case_justification: https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/SECURITY.md#threat-model (assets, actors and trust boundaries, threats and the mitigation of each) with the policies in the same file.
copyright_per_file_justification: Source files carry no copyright header; the LICENSE file covers the repository.
license_per_file_justification: Source files carry no SPDX-License-Identifier; the LICENSE file covers the repository.
require_2FA_justification: The GitHub organization requires two-factor authentication for every member.
secure_2FA_justification: GitHub enforces 2FA, but the project has not verified that no maintainer relies on SMS alone.
two_person_review_justification: Most changes are written and merged by the same maintainer today.
build_reproducible_justification: Two clean builds of the same commit produce byte-identical output (all 690 files of dist compared by SHA-256): https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/vite.config.ts
hardened_site_justification: The documentation site is served by GitHub Pages, which does not let a project set Content-Security-Policy, HSTS or X-Content-Type-Options headers.
security_review_justification: The maintainers reviewed the security requirements and boundaries in September 2026 and recorded the result as the threat model and policies in https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/SECURITY.md
code_review_standards_justification: https://github.com/brazilian-utils/javascript/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-review (how a pull request is reviewed, what CI already decides, the seven things a reviewer checks and what it takes to merge).
